device.category: semi-modular analogue synthesizer, desktop / Eurorack (80 HP)
device.based_on: Korg MS-20. The Behringer manual never names it; the module set, the patch panel and the high-pass plus low-pass filter pair are the MS-20's.

sources.title: K-2 Quick Start Guide
sources.note: Titled Quick Start Guide but carries 83 numbered controls, a Getting Started chapter that states the default modulation routings, a patch-panel block diagram, a MIDI message table, poly chain instructions and a full specifications table with envelope times and jack voltages.

sources.title: Korg MS-20 Owner's Manual
sources.note: A 44-page scan with no text layer, so not mined for this pass. It is the source that would settle the Hz/V keyboard scaling, the two filter circuits and the patch-panel normalling.

architecture.polyphony_mode: monophonic; poly chain across multiple units
architecture.summary: Two VCOs (VCO1 triangle / reverse saw / pulse / noise, VCO2 reverse saw / square / narrow pulse / ring) into a two-channel mixer, then through a high-pass filter and a low-pass filter in series, then a VCA. Both filters are 24 dB/octave and a single switch picks between two filter circuits. Modulation comes from a modulation generator (LFO) with two simultaneous morphing waveform outputs, and two envelope generators: EG1 (delay, attack, release) is normalled to oscillator pitch, EG2 (hold, attack, decay, sustain, release) to both filter cutoffs and to the VCA. A 27-jack patch panel exposes the whole thing, plus a sample and hold, a spare VCA, pink and white noise, a manual trigger switch, and an external signal processor that band-passes an incoming signal and converts it to pitch CV, an envelope and a trigger.

modules.name: Keyboard interface
modules.description: Turns incoming MIDI into pitch CV and a trigger. There is no keyboard on this model; notes arrive over the 5-pin DIN or USB. The keyboard CV output is specified as 0 to +8 V and exponential, which is the MS-20's Hz per volt convention rather than the 1 V per octave used by most of the rest of the market.

modules.name: Portamento
modules.description: Glide between successive notes, plus the master tune trim for the whole instrument.

modules.name: Oscillator pitch bus
modules.description: Where keyboard CV meets the two pitch patch points. VCO 1+2 CV IN drives both oscillators; VCO 2 CV IN drives only VCO2, which is how you detune or sequence the second oscillator on its own.

modules.name: Voltage Controlled Oscillator 1
modules.description: Primary oscillator. One waveform at a time from a four-position switch, one position of which is noise rather than a wave. Pulse width is adjustable when pulse is selected. Four octave scales from 32' to 4'.

frequency_hz.note: specifications give 16 Hz to 1.5 kHz at 8' with four overlapping ranges

modules.name: Voltage Controlled Oscillator 2
modules.description: Second oscillator, one octave up in scale range. Its fourth waveform position is RING, which is not a waveform at all but a ring modulation of the two oscillators. Its pitch can be offset independently of VCO1.

modules.name: VCO Mixer
modules.description: Two level controls, one per oscillator, summed into the filter chain.

modules.name: Modulation depth controls
modules.description: Six depth knobs in two panel sections. Each knob has a fixed source and a patch point that substitutes for it: the MG knobs take the modulation generator unless TOTAL is patched, the EG1 knob takes envelope 1 unless FREQ is patched, and each filter's EG2 knob takes envelope 2 unless that filter's CUTOFF FREQ jack is patched. TOTAL substitutes for the modulation generator in all four MG knobs at once, which is why it is called TOTAL.

modules.name: High-pass filter
modules.description: 24 dB/octave high-pass, attenuating below its cutoff. First filter in the chain, so it thins the fundamental and the lower harmonics before the low-pass gets the signal. PEAK is its resonance.

modules.name: Low-pass filter
modules.description: 24 dB/octave low-pass, attenuating above its cutoff. The FILTER 1/2 switch selects between two filter circuits; the manual does not say what distinguishes them.

modules.name: Voltage Controlled Amplifier
modules.description: Main amplifier at the end of the chain, opened by envelope 2. The INITIAL GAIN patch point is its modulation input.

modules.name: Patch panel VCA
modules.description: A second amplifier reachable only from the patch panel, with its own in, control in and out. The manual lists it separately from the main VCA block and the block diagram draws it as its own box in the lower row, so this file treats it as a distinct module.

modules.name: Modulation Generator
modules.description: The LFO. Two outputs run at once and one WAVEFORM knob shapes both: the first sweeps reverse sawtooth to triangle to sawtooth, the second sweeps wide pulse to square to narrow pulse. The first is bipolar at plus and minus 2.5 V, the second unipolar 0 to +5 V.

modules.name: Envelope Generator 1
modules.description: Delay, attack and release. Normalled to oscillator pitch, so its natural job is pitch sweeps. It has its own trigger input on the patch panel, separate from the global one.

modules.name: Envelope Generator 2
modules.description: Hold, attack, decay, sustain and release. Normalled to both filter cutoffs and to the VCA, so it is the main shaping envelope. Only its reversed output appears on the patch panel.

modules.name: Trigger routing
modules.description: Distributes the trigger that fires both envelopes. The keyboard trigger is the default source, the TRIG IN jack substitutes for it, TRIG OUT taps it for other gear, and the TRIG SW button generates one by hand. TRIG SW is also how poly chain mode is entered.

modules.name: Noise Generator
modules.description: Pink and white noise on separate outputs, both always available. White noise is also one of VCO1's four waveform positions.

modules.name: Sample & Hold
modules.description: Samples whatever is at its input each time a clock arrives and holds that value. Patch-only: the manual shows no pre-wired source for either its input or its clock, so it does nothing until cabled.

modules.name: External Signal Processor preamp
modules.description: Brings an external signal up to synth level. SIGNAL LEVEL sets the gain and its output is available before the band-pass filter.

modules.name: External Signal Processor band-pass
modules.description: Band-pass made from a low cut and a high cut control, used to isolate the part of the external signal that the pitch and envelope extractors should follow. Its output is available on its own jack.

modules.name: Frequency to voltage converter
modules.description: Tracks the pitch of the band-passed external signal and produces a control voltage from it, so an external instrument can play the oscillators. CV ADJUST scales the result.

modules.name: Envelope follower
modules.description: Produces a control voltage tracking the amplitude of the external signal. The PEAK LED shows when the input is peaking.

modules.name: External signal trigger extractor
modules.description: Fires a trigger whenever the external signal crosses the threshold set by THRESHOLD LEVEL, turning a drum track or a played note into something that can fire the envelopes. Its own LED shows the trigger.

modules.name: Output
modules.description: Master volume feeding the 3.5 mm SIGNAL OUT, the rear 1/4-inch OUTPUT and the headphone socket.

parameters.label: WAVEFORM
parameters.function: Selects the VCO1 waveform. The fourth position is noise rather than a wave, which replaces the oscillator with the noise generator in the mix.

parameters.label: PW
parameters.function: Pulse width, from square at one end to a narrow pulse at the other. Only has an effect with the pulse waveform selected. There is no pulse width modulation input anywhere on the instrument.

parameters.label: SCALE
parameters.function: Octave range for VCO1.

parameters.label: WAVEFORM

values.label: RING
values.meaning: ring modulation of VCO1 and VCO2

parameters.function: Selects the VCO2 waveform. The RING position is not a waveform: it replaces VCO2's output with the ring modulation of the two oscillators, so both are used to make one sound.

parameters.label: PITCH
parameters.function: Offsets VCO2's pitch relative to VCO1, for detuning or interval tuning. The span in semitones is not stated.

parameters.label: SCALE
parameters.function: Octave range for VCO2, one octave higher across the board than VCO1's.

parameters.label: PORTAMENTO
parameters.function: Glide time between notes.

parameters.label: MASTER TUNE
parameters.function: Overall tuning of the instrument.

parameters.label: VCO1 LEVEL
parameters.function: VCO1 level into the mixer.

parameters.label: VCO2 LEVEL
parameters.function: VCO2 level into the mixer.

parameters.label: MG/T.EXT (frequency)
parameters.function: Depth of oscillator frequency modulation from the modulation generator, or from whatever is patched into TOTAL, which substitutes for it.

parameters.label: EG1/EXT (frequency)
parameters.function: Depth of oscillator frequency modulation from envelope 1, or from whatever is patched into FREQ.

parameters.label: MG/T.EXT (high-pass cutoff)
parameters.function: Depth of high-pass cutoff modulation from the modulation generator, or from TOTAL.

parameters.label: EG2/EXT (high-pass cutoff)
parameters.function: Depth of high-pass cutoff modulation from envelope 2, or from the high-pass CUTOFF FREQ jack.

parameters.label: MG/T.EXT (low-pass cutoff)
parameters.function: Depth of low-pass cutoff modulation from the modulation generator, or from TOTAL.

parameters.label: EG2/EXT (low-pass cutoff)
parameters.function: Depth of low-pass cutoff modulation from envelope 2, or from the low-pass CUTOFF FREQ jack.

parameters.label: CUTOFF FREQUENCY (high-pass)
parameters.function: High-pass cutoff. Everything below it is attenuated, which thins out the fundamental.

parameters.label: PEAK (high-pass)
parameters.function: High-pass resonance: emphasis at the cutoff frequency.

parameters.label: CUTOFF FREQUENCY (low-pass)
parameters.function: Low-pass cutoff. Everything above it is attenuated.

parameters.label: PEAK (low-pass)
parameters.function: Low-pass resonance: emphasis at the cutoff frequency.

parameters.label: FILTER 1/2
parameters.function: Selects between two filter circuits. The manual says only 'filter type 1 or 2' and never explains the difference; on the MS-20 this is the early Korg 35 design versus the later one, and they sound audibly different at high resonance. The switch governs both filters, not just the low-pass.
parameters.note: That it applies to both filters, and what the two circuits are, are both inferred; the manual says neither.

parameters.label: WAVEFORM

values.meaning: output 1 fully counter-clockwise; output 2 is a wide pulse
output 1 at centre; output 2 is a square
output 1 fully clockwise; output 2 is a narrow pulse

parameters.function: One knob shapes both modulation generator outputs at once. Sweeping it takes the first output from reverse sawtooth through triangle to sawtooth, and simultaneously takes the second from wide pulse through square to narrow pulse. The two outputs are always both live on their own jacks.

parameters.label: FREQUENCY
parameters.function: Modulation generator rate.

parameters.label: DELAY TIME
parameters.function: Time between the trigger arriving and the attack starting.

parameters.label: ATTACK TIME
parameters.function: Time for envelope 1 to reach maximum after a note is played.

parameters.label: RELEASE TIME
parameters.function: Fall time after the note is released.

parameters.label: HOLD TIME
parameters.function: The manual describes this as extending how long the trigger signal is held, which would affect both envelopes; the specifications list it as envelope generator 2's hold time. Modelled here on EG2, following the specifications.
parameters.note: The two statements in the manual disagree about what HOLD acts on. See source_inconsistencies.

parameters.label: ATTACK TIME
parameters.function: Attack time of envelope 2.

parameters.label: DECAY TIME
parameters.function: Decay time after the attack completes.

parameters.label: SUSTAIN LEVEL
parameters.function: Level held after attack and decay for as long as the note is held.

parameters.label: RELEASE TIME
parameters.function: Fall time after the note is released.

parameters.label: VOLUME
parameters.function: Overall output level of the synthesizer.

parameters.label: TRIG SW
parameters.function: Generates a trigger by hand, available at TRIG SW OUT. Pressing it four times quickly after power-up, while the ON LED is flashing, toggles poly chain mode.

parameters.label: SIGNAL LEVEL
parameters.function: Input gain for the external signal.

parameters.label: LOW CUT FREQ
parameters.function: Lower edge of the external signal processor's band-pass filter.

parameters.label: HIGH CUT FREQ
parameters.function: Upper edge of the band-pass filter.

parameters.label: CV ADJUST
parameters.function: Scales the control voltage produced by the frequency to voltage converter, which is how you get an external instrument to track in tune when driving the oscillators.

parameters.label: THRESHOLD LEVEL
parameters.function: Level the external signal must cross before a trigger is produced.

parameters.label: MIDI CHANNEL
parameters.function: MIDI receive channel, set by four rear DIP switches. The 16 combinations are printed in the manual.

parameters.label: POWER
parameters.function: Turns the synthesizer on and off. Make all connections before switching on.

parameters.label: Poly chain mode

access.gesture: press TRIG SW four times quickly after power-up, while the ON LED flashes

parameters.function: Chains several units so they share notes. Entered or left by pressing TRIG SW four times quickly after power-up while the ON LED is flashing, and also configurable with Behringer's SynthTool application. The ON LED turns red while it is active.

indicators.label: ON
indicators.function: Shows that power is applied and the rear switch is on, and doubles as the system mode display: amber for normal mode, red for poly chain mode. It flashes for a moment after power-up, which is the window in which TRIG SW toggles poly chain.

indicators.label: LED (modulation generator)
indicators.function: Blinks at the modulation generator rate.

indicators.label: LED (envelope generator)
indicators.function: Shows envelope generator action. Listed in the specifications only; the numbered controls do not mention it.

indicators.label: PEAK
indicators.function: Lights when the external input signal is peaking.

indicators.label: LED (trigger)
indicators.function: Lights when the external signal processor is producing a trigger.

led_legend.rule: Only one LED on the K-2 carries a colour code: the ON LED, which reports the system mode as well as power. Every other indicator is single-colour and means only that the thing it sits next to is active.
led_legend.note: Taken from the System Mode LED table printed beside the poly chain instructions. The colours of the other LEDs are read from the panel artwork, not documented.

ports.label: MIDI IN
ports.function: Receives MIDI from a keyboard, sequencer or computer on the channel set at the rear.

ports.label: SIGNAL OUT
ports.function: Main line-level audio output on a 3.5 mm jack.

ports.label: PHONES
ports.function: Headphone output. Turn the volume down before putting them on.

ports.label: TOTAL
ports.function: Substitutes for the modulation generator in all four MG/T.EXT depth knobs at once, so one cable re-sources both oscillators and both filters.

ports.label: FREQ

electrical.note: specifications say -3 V to +3 V for the VCO 1+2 frequency input while the panel is printed -5 V to +5 V

ports.function: Substitutes for envelope 1 in the EG1/EXT frequency depth knob, modulating both oscillators.

ports.label: EXT SIGNAL IN
ports.function: Injects external audio into the filter chain, joining the oscillator mix at the high-pass input.
ports.note: The block diagram puts this jack on the line between the mixer and the high-pass filter. Whether it sums with the mixer or breaks it is not stated.

ports.label: CUTOFF FREQ (high-pass)
ports.function: Substitutes for envelope 2 in the high-pass EG2/EXT depth knob.

ports.label: CUTOFF FREQ (low-pass)
ports.function: Substitutes for envelope 2 in the low-pass EG2/EXT depth knob.

ports.label: INITIAL GAIN
ports.function: Modulation input for the main VCA.
ports.note: The manual calls it a modulation input but does not say whether it adds to envelope 2 or replaces it.

ports.label: MG OUT (reverse saw / triangle / saw)
ports.function: First modulation generator output, shaped by the WAVEFORM knob. Bipolar.

ports.label: MG OUT (wide pulse / square / narrow)
ports.function: Second modulation generator output, shaped by the same WAVEFORM knob. Unipolar, so useful as a clock or gate.

ports.label: EG 1 OUT
ports.function: Envelope 1 output.

ports.label: EG 1 REV OUT
ports.function: Envelope 1 inverted: falls from +5 V to 0 where the normal output rises.

ports.label: EG1 TRIG IN
ports.function: Fires envelope 1 on its own, independently of the global trigger.

ports.label: EG 2 REV OUT
ports.function: Envelope 2 inverted. There is no jack for envelope 2's normal output.

ports.label: VCO 2 CV IN
ports.function: Pitch CV for VCO2 alone, which is how the second oscillator is played or sequenced separately.

ports.label: VCO 1+2 CV IN
ports.function: Pitch CV for both oscillators, substituting for the keyboard.

ports.label: KBD CV OUT

electrical.scaling: Hz per volt (inferred from 'exponential' and from the MS-20 original; not stated)

ports.function: The keyboard control voltage, for driving other gear or patching back in.

ports.label: TRIG OUT
ports.function: The trigger that fires the envelopes, tapped for other gear.

ports.label: TRIG IN
ports.function: External trigger, substituting for the keyboard's own.

ports.label: S&H IN
ports.function: Signal to be sampled.

ports.label: CLOCK
ports.function: Clock telling the sample and hold when to take a reading.

ports.label: S&H OUT
ports.function: Stepped output of the sample and hold.

ports.label: VCA IN
ports.function: Input of the patch panel VCA.

ports.label: VCA CONTROL INPUT
ports.function: Gain control for the patch panel VCA.

ports.label: VCA OUT
ports.function: Output of the patch panel VCA. The manual calls it a control output, which does not match the block diagram or the specifications.

ports.label: PINK
ports.function: Pink noise output.

ports.label: WHITE
ports.function: White noise output.

ports.label: TRIG SW OUT
ports.function: Output of the manual trigger switch.

ports.label: SIGNAL IN
ports.function: External audio into the signal processor.

ports.label: OUT (pre-filter)
ports.function: The amplified external signal before the band-pass filter.

ports.label: OUT (post-filter)
ports.function: The external signal after the band-pass filter.

ports.label: F-V CV OUT
ports.function: Pitch CV extracted from the external signal, for playing the oscillators from an instrument or a voice.

ports.label: ENV OUT
ports.function: Envelope follower output tracking the loudness of the external signal.

ports.label: TRIG OUT (ESP)
ports.function: Trigger produced whenever the external signal crosses the threshold.

ports.label: OUTPUT
ports.function: Main output on a 1/4-inch jack, for amplifiers and interfaces.

ports.label: MIDI THRU
ports.function: Passes through whatever arrives at MIDI IN. This is how units are daisy-chained for poly chain.

ports.label: USB PORT
ports.function: Class-compliant USB MIDI in and out, no driver needed on Windows or macOS.

ports.label: DC INPUT
ports.function: 12 V DC from the supplied adaptor only, which takes 100 to 240 V at 50 or 60 Hz.

connections.note: Keyboard CV is the default pitch source for both oscillators. Patching VCO 1+2 CV IN takes over; patching VCO 2 CV IN takes over for VCO2 only. How the two patch points interact with each other is not documented.
The modulation generator's first output is the default source for all four MG/T.EXT knobs.
With RING selected, VCO2's output becomes the ring modulation of the two oscillators, so VCO1 feeds it.
The noise position on VCO1's waveform switch substitutes noise for the oscillator. Which noise colour it uses is not stated; white is assumed.
Envelope 2 opens the VCA. Whether the INITIAL GAIN jack replaces it or sums with it is not stated.

behaviours.name: Patch panel overrides the internal wiring
behaviours.rule: The manual describes the patch panel as an interactive block diagram: the printed lines between blocks are the internal connections, and patching a cable into a jack overrides the connection drawn into it. Nothing needs patching for the instrument to make a sound.

behaviours.name: Default modulation sources
behaviours.rule: With nothing patched, oscillator frequency is modulated by the modulation generator and envelope 1, and both filter cutoffs by the modulation generator and envelope 2. Each depth knob is labelled with both its internal source and the EXT that replaces it, which is why the knobs read MG/T.EXT and EG1/EXT rather than just MG and EG1.

behaviours.name: TOTAL is a four-way substitution
behaviours.rule: One cable into TOTAL replaces the modulation generator as the source for all four MG/T.EXT knobs at once: VCO1, VCO2, high-pass cutoff and low-pass cutoff. The individual FREQ and CUTOFF FREQ jacks replace only their own knob's source.

behaviours.name: Two filters in series
behaviours.rule: The high-pass comes first and the low-pass second, both 24 dB/octave. Setting the high-pass above the low-pass narrows the passband to nothing; setting them close together with both PEAK controls up gives the band-pass scream the MS-20 is known for. The manual's phrase 'emphasis at the crossover frequency' points at the same thing.

behaviours.name: RING is not a waveform
behaviours.rule: Selecting RING on VCO2's waveform switch replaces its output with the ring modulation of VCO1 and VCO2, so both oscillators are consumed to produce one inharmonic voice. Detuning VCO2 then changes the character rather than the interval.

behaviours.name: Noise as an oscillator waveform
behaviours.rule: VCO1's fourth waveform position substitutes noise for the oscillator. Noise is therefore available two ways: mixed and filtered through VCO1's channel, or straight off the pink and white jacks on the patch panel. The manual does not say which colour the VCO1 position uses.

behaviours.name: Envelope division of labour
behaviours.rule: EG1 has delay, attack and release only, and is normalled to pitch. EG2 has hold, attack, decay, sustain and release, and is normalled to both cutoffs and to the VCA. Both fire from the same trigger unless EG1 TRIG IN is patched, which gives EG1 its own.

behaviours.name: Inverted envelope outputs
behaviours.rule: Both envelopes have a reversed output on the patch panel: EG1 falls from +5 V to 0 where the normal output rises, and EG2's reversed output swings between -2.5 V and +2.5 V. EG1's normal output has a jack; EG2's does not, so envelope 2 is only available inverted unless you use its internal routings.

behaviours.name: Keyboard CV is Hz per volt
behaviours.rule: The keyboard CV output is specified as 0 to +8 V and exponential, and the oscillator CV inputs accept 0 to +8 V. An exponential response means volts map to frequency rather than to pitch, which is the MS-20's Hz per volt standard. This matters when patching to other synthesizers: a 1 V/octave module will not track correctly without a converter. The manual never uses the phrase Hz per volt.

behaviours.name: Modulation generator morphing
behaviours.rule: There is one waveform knob and two outputs, and the knob shapes both at the same time. It is a continuous sweep, not a switch, so intermediate shapes between reverse sawtooth and triangle, or between square and narrow pulse, are valid settings.

behaviours.name: External signal processor
behaviours.rule: An external signal is amplified, band-passed, and then split three ways: a frequency to voltage converter produces pitch CV, an envelope follower produces a loudness CV, and a threshold comparator produces triggers. Patch those three into pitch, cutoff and the envelopes and the synthesizer plays from a guitar, a voice or a drum track. None of the three outputs has an internal destination, so the section does nothing until it is cabled.
behaviours.note: That the three outputs have no internal destination is read off the block diagram, not stated.

behaviours.name: Poly chain
behaviours.rule: Units share a MIDI channel and are daisy-chained through MIDI THRU, with notes distributed between them. Mode is toggled by pressing TRIG SW four times quickly during the post-power-up window while the ON LED flashes, or set with Behringer's SynthTool application. The ON LED shows red while poly chain is active and amber otherwise. The manual does not say how many units can be chained; the cover claims 16 voices.

behaviours.name: Warm-up
behaviours.rule: The manual asks for 15 minutes or more of warm-up before recording or playing live, longer from cold, for the analogue circuits to reach tuning stability. A faithful model may want slow pitch drift that settles over that period.

behaviours.name: Patch point voltage limits
behaviours.rule: The manual warns twice that the 3.5 mm inputs must not be overloaded and that outputs should only reach inputs that can take their voltage, on pain of damage. The ranges are in the specifications: mostly -5 V to +5 V, 0 to +8 V on the oscillator and keyboard CV paths, and 3 Vpp on the external signal input.

source_inconsistencies: Item 29 describes HOLD TIME as extending the trigger signal, which would affect both envelopes, while the specifications list it as envelope generator 2's hold time. This file follows the specifications.
The panel prints -5 V to +5 V beside the FREQ jack, but the specifications give the VCO 1+2 frequency input as -3 V to +3 V.
The specifications list an 'EG 2 out' at -2.5 V to +2.5 V, but there is no EG 2 OUT jack; only EG 2 REV OUT exists on the panel and in the numbered controls.
Item 60 calls VCA OUT a control output, while the block diagram and the specifications treat it as the amplifier's signal output.
The Envelope Generator Section heading in the numbered controls has no numbered item for the EG action LED, which the specifications do list.
The manual is titled Quick Start Guide throughout but contains a full controls reference and specifications.
Item 23 is described as indicating 'the current rate' of the modulation generator in English and 'the active state' in Spanish; it is a rate blinker.

modelling_gaps.detail: If the keyboard CV really is Hz/V, every pitch calculation in a model of this instrument differs from the 1 V/octave assumption used in the other files in this collection. Confirming it from the MS-20 manual should be the first job.
Two selectable filters and no description of either. On the MS-20 the difference is audible and mostly in the resonance behaviour, which is exactly what is unspecified here.
PEAK is described only as emphasis at cutoff. Nothing on whether either filter self-oscillates, which on the MS-20 both do.
Every knob is 0 to 10. Physical end points exist only for the envelope times, the LFO rate and the filter cutoff sweep; the mapping between knob position and value is never given.
16 Hz to 1.5 kHz at 8' with four overlapping ranges, but no statement of what each scale position does to that, and no fine tune beyond VCO2's PITCH knob.
Described as square to narrow with no percentages and no modulation input, so PWM is not available on this instrument at all.
No statement of whether it is a true four-quadrant multiplier, and no level relationship between the RING position and the other three waveforms.
No frequency range for the band-pass, no tracking range or latency for the frequency to voltage converter, no time constants for the envelope follower.
Times are given but not segment shapes. Exponential RC is likely.

The uploaded original is a 44-page scan with no text layer. OCR would likely settle the Hz/V scaling, the filter circuits, the patch panel normalling and the ring modulator, in the same way the ARP 2600 manual would for the 2600 file.
